cues.en: Like a lot of kids born in the early seventies, I had the good fortune to be raised by hippies.
cues.zh: 就像许多七十年代初出生的孩子一样，我很幸运是由嬉皮士养大的。

cues.en: One of my childhood heroes was Stewart Brand.
cues.zh: 我童年时的偶像之一是 Stewart Brand。

cues.en: Stuart is not only one of the originary hippies, he's also one of the first modern environmentalists
cues.zh: Stuart 不仅是最早的一批嬉皮士之一，他也是六七十年代最早的现代环保主义者之一。

cues.en: of the nineteen sixties and seventies.
cues.zh: 上世纪六七十年代的。

cues.en: As a young boy,
cues.zh: 作为一个小男孩，

cues.en: one of my favorite memories is playing cooperative games that Stuart designed as an antidote to the Vietnam War.
cues.zh: 我最美好的回忆之一就是玩 Stuart 设计的合作游戏，以此来作为对越战的一种对抗。

cues.en: I'm from a long line of Christian pacifists known as Mennonites. And every August, we would go as kids to remember the US government's atomic bombing of Japan by lighting candles
cues.zh: 我出身于一个被称为门诺派的基督教和平主义世族。每年八月，我们还是孩子的时候都会去点燃蜡烛，纪念美国政府对日本投下的原子弹，

cues.en: and sending them on boats onto Bittersweet Park.
cues.zh: 然后把它们放到 Bittersweet 公园的小船上顺水漂流。

cues.en: As I graduated from high school throughout college, I brought
cues.zh: 从高中毕业到上大学的这段时间里，我曾带过

cues.en: many delegations to Central America to bring diplomacy,
cues.zh: 许多代表团去中美洲开展外交，

cues.en: seek peace,
cues.zh: 寻求和平，

cues.en: and also to support local farmer cooperatives in Guatemala, Central America, Nicaragua.
cues.zh: 同时也支持危地马拉和中美洲尼加拉瓜当地的农民合作社。

cues.en: And over time, as I've traveled around the world, been through many small communities on all the different continents,
cues.zh: 随着时间的推移，当我走遍世界各地、去过各大洲的许多小型社区后，

cues.en: I've come to appreciate that the young people I interview, they don't wanna be stuck in the village. They don't wanna spend their whole lives chopping wood and hauling wood. They wanna go to the city for opportunity. Most of them do. For education, for work.
cues.zh: 我渐渐意识到，我采访的年轻人并不想困在村子里。他们不想一辈子都在劈柴挑水。他们想去城市寻找机遇。大多数人都这样想。为了教育，为了工作。

cues.en: And what I've realized is that that process of urbanization,
cues.zh: 而我所意识到的是，城市化这个进程，

cues.en: of moving to the city, is actually very positive for nature. It allows the natural environment to come back. It allows for the
cues.zh: 也就是向城市迁移，实际上对大自然是非常有利的。它让自然环境得以恢复。它让

cues.en: Central African mountain gorillas, for example, an important endangered species,
cues.zh: 例如中非山地大猩猩这样一个重要的濒危物种，

cues.en: to have the habitat that they need to survive and thrive.
cues.zh: 拥有生存和繁衍所需的栖息地。

cues.en: And of course, in that process,
cues.zh: 当然，在这个过程中，

cues.en: you've got to go vertical. So even places like Hong Kong, you see, can spare their natural environment around the city, but it requires a huge amount of energy to go up. And so the big challenge of our time is how do you get plentiful,
cues.zh: 你必须向上发展。所以，即使像香港这样的地方，你看，也可以保护城市周边的自然环境，但这需要消耗巨量能源来向上发展。因此，我们这个时代面临的重大挑战就是：如何获得充足的、

cues.en: reliable electricity and energy
cues.zh: 可靠的电力和能源

cues.en: without destroying the climate?
cues.zh: 同时又不破坏气候？

cues.en: Well, I started out as an anti nuclear activist, and I quickly got involved in advocating for renewable energy. So at the early part of the the... This this century,
cues.zh: 我一开始是一名反核活动人士，很快就参与到倡导可再生能源的工作中。21世纪初，

cues.en: I helped to start a labor union and environmentalist
cues.zh: 我帮助发起了一个劳工组织与环保人士的

cues.en: alliance called the Apollo Alliance. And we pushed for a big investment in clean energy, solar, wind, electric cars.
cues.zh: 联盟，叫作 Apollo Alliance。我们推动对清洁能源进行大规模投资，包括太阳能、风能和电动汽车。

cues.en: And the investment idea was picked up by president Obama. And during his time in office,
cues.zh: Obama 总统接受了这一投资理念。在他任职期间，

cues.en: he invested about a $150,000,000,000,
cues.zh: 他投入了大约1500亿美元，

cues.en: to make solar and wind and electric cars much cheaper than they were. And that was having a lot of success, but we were starting to notice some challenges. Some of them you're familiar with. Solar and wind generate electricity
cues.zh: 让太阳能、风能和电动汽车的成本大幅低于原来的水平。这取得了很大成功，但我们也开始注意到一些挑战。其中有些你们很熟悉。太阳能和风能发电

cues.en: about 10 to 30% of the time. So we're dependent on on the weather for solar and wind. There were other problems we were noticing though. Sometimes these sources of electricity generate too much power. And you hear a lot of hype about batteries, but we actually don't have sufficient storage, even in California where we have a lot of investment, a lot of
cues.zh: 大约只有10%到30%的时间。因此，太阳能和风能都依赖天气。不过，我们还发现了其他问题。有时，这些电力来源产生的电力太多了。你经常会听到关于电池的各种宣传，但实际上，即使是在加州这样投入了大量资金、很多

cues.en: Silicon Valley types putting money into battery storage technology. So we're trying to figure out how do you manage all those renewables.
cues.zh: 硅谷人士都在投资电池储能技术的地方，我们仍然没有足够的储能能力。所以，我们正在设法弄清楚该如何管理所有这些可再生能源。

cues.en: And while we were struggling with this problem,
cues.zh: 正当我们为这个问题苦苦挣扎时，

cues.en: around 2005,
cues.zh: 大约在 2005 年，

cues.en: Stewart Brand came out and he said,
cues.zh: 斯图尔特·布兰德（Stewart Brand）站出来说，

cues.en: we should rethink nuclear power. And this was like a shock to the system. I mean, for me and for all of my friends.
cues.zh: 我们应该重新思考核电。这简直像给整个系统带来了一记重击。我是说，对我以及我所有的朋友来说都是如此。

cues.en: I mean, Stuart was one of the first big advocates of solar energy anywhere. In the late sixties and early seventies, he advised the governor of California.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，斯图尔特曾是最早大力倡导太阳能的人之一。在 60 年代末和 70 年代初，他曾担任加州州长的顾问。

cues.en: But he said, look, you know, we've been trying to do solar for a long time. And at the time, he said we have less than, you know, less than a half a percent of our electricity globally comes from solar, about 2% from wind, and the majority comes from nuclear and hydro. And he said, look, you know,
cues.zh: 但他说，听着，你知道的，我们推广太阳能已经很久了。当时他说，全球由太阳能提供的电力连半个百分点都不到，风能大约占 2%，而绝大部分来自核能和水能。并且他说，听着，你知道的，

cues.en: despite what you might think, according to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, nuclear actually produces four times less carbon emissions than solar does.
cues.zh: 不管你怎么想，根据政府间气候变化专门委员会（IPCC）的数据，核能产生的碳排放实际上比太阳能还要少四倍。

cues.en: And in fact, that's why they recommended in their most recent report that achieving deep cuts in emissions is going require a more intensive use of renewables,
cues.zh: 事实上，这也是为什么他们在最近的报告中建议，要大幅削减碳排放，将需要更密集地使用可再生能源、

cues.en: nuclear and carbon capture and storage.
cues.zh: 核能以及碳捕获与封存技术。

cues.en: Well, let's take a closer look at Germany.
cues.zh: 好吧，让我们仔细看看德国。

cues.en: So Germany gets the majority of its electricity and, of course, all of its transportation fuels from fossil fuels. So just the electrical sector, last year Germany got 40% of its electricity from coal.
cues.zh: 德国的大部分电力，以及当然所有的交通燃料，都来自化石燃料。就电力部门而言，去年德国有 40% 的电力来自煤炭。

cues.en: It got 12% from natural gas, 13% from nuclear,
cues.zh: 其中 12% 来自天然气，13% 来自核能，

cues.en: 12% from wind, and about 6% from solar. So to go from 18% wind and solar to a 100%,
cues.zh: 12% 来自风能，大约 6% 来自太阳能。因此，要从 18% 的风能和太阳能跨越到 100%，

cues.en: you actually have to go beyond that. If you're replacing all of the transportation sector with electric cars, you're looking at something more like a 150%.
cues.zh: 你实际上得超越这个数字。如果你用电动汽车取代整个交通运输行业，你所需要的比例大概得达到 150% 左右。

cues.en: So Germany has done a lot to invest in renewables and to innovate solar and wind, but that's still a pretty steep climb. That's even before you get to the question of storage.
cues.zh: 德国已经为可再生能源投入很多，也在太阳能和风能上做了很多创新，但这仍然是相当陡峭的爬坡。这还没算上储能问题。

cues.en: So... Well, let's take a look at what happened last year.
cues.zh: 那么……好吧，我们来看看去年发生了什么。

cues.en: Last year, Germany installed 4% more solar panels, but it generated 3% less electricity from solar. And even when I'm in meetings with energy experts, I'll ask people if they can make a guess as to why that is, and you'd be shocked at how many energy experts have no idea.
cues.zh: 去年，德国多安装了4%的太阳能板，但太阳能发电量却少了3%。甚至在我和能源专家开会时，我会问他们能不能猜猜为什么会这样，你会惊讶地发现，很多能源专家根本不知道。

cues.en: It just wasn't very sunny last year in Germany.
cues.zh: 原因就是去年德国日照不太充足。

cues.en: Well, that probably meant though then that it was windier. Right? Because if it's not as sunny, then maybe there's some more wind and those two things can balance each other out.
cues.zh: 那你可能会想，这是不是意味着风更多了。对吧？因为如果日照没那么充足，也许风就会多一点，这两者可以相互平衡。

cues.en: In truth, Germany had sold 11%
cues.zh: 事实上，德国多卖出了11%

cues.en: more wind turbines in 2016,
cues.zh: 的风力涡轮机，那是在2016年，

cues.en: but it got 2% less electricity from wind.
cues.zh: 但风力发电量却少了2%。

cues.en: Same story, just not very windy last year.
cues.zh: 同样的问题，去年风也不太足。

cues.en: So you might think, well, we just have to do a lot more solar and wind so that in years where there's not a lot of sunlight and wind, that there's more electricity from those energy sources.
cues.zh: 所以你可能会想，那我们就得多建很多太阳能和风能，这样在光照和风都不多的年份，这些能源也能发出更多电。

cues.en: So Germany's plan is to increase by 50% the amount of electricity Germany gets from solar. That would take you from, you know, 40 gigawatts to about 60 gigawatts in 2030.
cues.zh: 德国的计划是把太阳能发电量提高50%。也就是从你知道的40吉瓦，提高到2030年的约60吉瓦。

cues.en: But if you have a year like 2016,
cues.zh: 但如果遇到像2016年这样的年份，

cues.en: that means that you'll still only be getting around 9% of your total electricity from solar. And this is in really the biggest solar country in the world. I mean, Germany is really the powerhouse of renewable electricity.
cues.zh: 那意味着太阳能仍然只能占到总发电量的9%左右。而这还是在全球最大的太阳能国家。我是说，德国确实是可再生能源发电的强国。

cues.en: So the obvious response is, well, we'll just put it all in batteries. We hear so much about batteries. You would think that we just have a huge amount of storage.
cues.zh: 所以显而易见的答案是，我们干脆全放进电池里。我们听到那么多关于电池的说法，会以为我们已经有巨量储能了。

cues.en: Well, our staff took a look at the numbers in California, and what we discovered is that we have twenty three minutes of electricity storage for California's grid. But that require... To get that twenty three minutes requires using every
cues.zh: 嗯，我们的团队看了加州的数字，发现我们为加州电网只有23分钟的电力储存。但这需要……要得到这23分钟，就需要用上

cues.en: battery and every car and truck in the state,
cues.zh: 这个州的每一块电池，以及每一辆汽车和卡车，

cues.en: which as you can imagine is not super practical if you're trying to get somewhere.
cues.zh: 你可以想象，如果你正想赶路，这可不是特别实际。

cues.en: And Germany might be a little bit different, but not very different from that.
cues.zh: 德国可能稍有不同，但差别也不大。

cues.en: Well, most people are aware that to make this transition towards renewables,
cues.zh: 嗯，大多数人都知道，要实现向可再生能源的转型，

cues.en: Germany has been spending a lot more on electricity.
cues.zh: 德国在电力上的支出一直高得多。

cues.en: And you can see electricity prices in Germany rose about 50% over the last ten years.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，德国电价在过去十年上涨了约50%。

cues.en: Today, German electricity is about two times more expensive than electricity is in France. And you might think, look, that's a small price to pay for dealing with climate change, and I would agree with that. Spending a little bit more money on energy, especially for those of us in the rich world, is a decent thing to do to avert some of the catastrophic possibilities
cues.zh: 今天，德国电价大约是法国的两倍。你可能觉得，看，为应对气候变化付这点小代价不算什么，我同意。在能源上多花一点钱，尤其对我们富裕世界的人来说，是避免某些灾难性可能的正当之举

cues.en: of global warming.
cues.zh: 全球变暖的。

cues.en: But the interesting thing is is that when you look and when you compare France and Germany in terms of their electricity,
cues.zh: 但有趣的是，当你观察并比较法国和德国的电力时，

cues.en: France gets 93%
cues.zh: 法国有93%

cues.en: of their electricity from clean energy sources, mostly hydro and nuclear.
cues.zh: 的电力来自清洁能源，主要是水电和核能。

cues.en: Germany gets just 46%,
cues.zh: 德国只拿到46%，

cues.en: like about half.
cues.zh: 大概一半。

cues.en: And here's the real shocking thing.
cues.zh: 真正令人震惊的是，

cues.en: German carbon emissions have actually been going up since 2009.
cues.zh: 德国的碳排放自2009年以来其实一直在上升。

cues.en: They have increased
cues.zh: 过去两年

cues.en: over the last two years, and they may increase this year as well. And German carbon emissions have declined since the nineteen nineties,
cues.zh: 它们增加了，而且今年可能还会增加。德国的碳排放自上世纪九十年代以来确实下降了，

cues.en: but most of that is just due to the fact that after reunification,
cues.zh: 但这大部分只是因为两德统一后，

cues.en: Germany just took offline all of those inefficient coal plants in East Germany. Most of that reduction is just due to that. And
cues.zh: 德国直接关停了东德所有那些低效的燃煤电厂。大部分减排就只是因为这个。

cues.en: let's take a look at last year. One of the things that really quickly can reduce emissions is switching from coal to natural gas because natural gas is about half of the carbon intensity of coal.
cues.zh: 再看看去年。能快速减排的办法之一是从煤转天然气，因为天然气的碳强度大约是煤的一半。

cues.en: And that would have resulted in a pretty significant reduction in German carbon emissions last year, except for the fact that Germany took offline nuclear.
cues.zh: 这本来会让德国去年的碳排放显著下降，只不过德国同时关停了核电。

cues.en: And when it did that, it meant that the emissions actually ended up going up again.
cues.zh: 这一关，就导致排放最终又升了回去。

cues.en: Now, there's some questions about what about the future? So if we just do more solar and wind, won't it kind of all work itself out?
cues.zh: 那未来怎么办？如果我们就多搞太阳能和风能，是不是自然而然就解决了？

cues.en: Well, one of the biggest challenges to this has come from somebody here in Germany who
cues.zh: 这方面最大的挑战之一，来自德国本地一位

cues.en: is not a pro nuclear person at all, is an
cues.zh: 完全不是支持核电的人，他是一位

cues.en: energy analyst and economist named Leon Hirth. And what he finds is that that problem I described earlier where sometimes you have too much wind at certain parts of the day or certain parts of the year or too much solar and not clear what to do with it, that that reduces the economic value of wind and solar. So wind actually, the value of it reduces 40%
cues.zh: 能源分析师和经济学家，叫Leon Hirth。他发现，我前面说的那个问题——有时候一天中某些时段或一年中某些时候风太大、或者太阳能太多，不知道怎么处理——这会降低风能和太阳能的经济价值。风能的价值实际上会下降40%，

cues.en: once it gets to be 30% of your electricity.
cues.zh: 一旦它占到电力结构的30%。

cues.en: And solar, it's even more dramatic. It actually declines by half when it gets to just 15%.
cues.zh: 太阳能就更夸张了。当渗透率仅达到 15% 时，它实际上就会减半。

cues.en: So one of the things you hear though is that, well,
cues.zh: 不过你经常会听到的一种说法是，

cues.en: we can do a solar roof like really fast. I mean, solar is fast. You just put it up on one day and you've installed the thing, whereas it takes like ten years or five years depending on where you are to build a nuclear plant. And so that makes sense. You'd think, well, if we do solar and wind, you can just go a lot faster. But this was actually studied in an important article for the journal Science last year. One of the lead authors... One of the authors was James Hansen, the famous climate scientist.
cues.zh: 我们安装太阳能屋顶速度极快。我是说，太阳能很快。你只要花一天时间把它搭起来就装好了，而建一座核电站却需要五到十年，具体取决于你在哪里。所以这很合理。你会想，如果搞太阳能和风能，进度就能快得多。但去年《科学》杂志上的一篇重要文章其实专门研究过这一点。主要作者之一……其中一位作者是著名的气候科学家 James Hansen。

cues.en: And what they found is that even when you combine solar and wind,
cues.zh: 而他们的研究发现是，即使把太阳能和风能结合起来，

cues.en: you just get a lot less
cues.zh: 你得到的

cues.en: clean electricity than when you do nuclear. And that goes for Germany as well as The United States. So what they did is they just compared
cues.zh: 清洁电力也远比搞核电少得多。无论是德国还是美国都是如此。所以他们所做的，只是对比了

cues.en: the ten years of the most deployment of those two technologies, solar and wind versus nuclear. And it's a pretty stark comparison.
cues.zh: 这两种技术（太阳能和风能）与核电最大规模部署的那十年。这个对比非常鲜明。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: I can see what you're... I can imagine what you're thinking because this what I was sort of thinking. It was like, well, this sounds like I now have to really reconsider my attitudes around nuclear power. But then what about Chernobyl? What about Fukushima? What about all the nuclear waste? Those are really reasonable questions to ask.
cues.zh: 我能看出你在……我能猜到你在想什么，因为我以前也这么想过。就觉得，听起来我好像真的得重新考虑我对核电的态度了。但切尔诺贝利怎么办？福岛怎么办？所有的核废料怎么办？这些确实都是很合理的问题。

cues.en: And in fact, when I was starting to ask them, there were other people that were starting to change their mind. One of the ones who I was most impressed by and was very influential
cues.zh: 事实上，当我开始问他们时，还有其他人也开始改变看法。其中让我印象最深刻、影响也很大的一位

cues.en: is a British newspaper columnist named George Mambiat.
cues.zh: 是一位名叫乔治·蒙比亚特的英国报纸专栏作家。

cues.en: George Mambiat wrote a column shortly after Fukushima where he went through the scientific research on radiation and what he wrote was,
cues.zh: 福岛事件后不久，乔治·蒙比亚特写了一篇专栏文章，他仔细研究了关于辐射的科学研究，他写道：

cues.en: The anti nuclear movement to which I once belonged
cues.zh: 我曾经所属的反核运动

cues.en: has misled the world about the impacts of radiation on human health.
cues.zh: 一直在辐射对人类健康影响的问题上误导世界。

cues.en: I write some pretty harsh things sometimes, but this was a pretty strong column.
cues.zh: 有时我会写一些相当严厉的东西，但这篇专栏文章力度确实很大。

cues.en: He was talking to a number of scientists that actually have studied the big accidents.
cues.zh: 他当时正与许多真正研究过重大事故的科学家交谈。

cues.en: One of them is Geri Thomas from Imperial College in London.
cues.zh: 其中一位是来自伦敦帝国学院的吉里·托马斯。

cues.en: Geri started something called the Chernobyl Tissue Bank out of her concern for the accident
cues.zh: 吉里出于对事故的关注，发起了一个名为“切尔诺贝利组织库”的项目

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: totally independent
cues.zh: 完全独立

cues.en: professor
cues.zh: 担任

cues.en: of pathology at Imperial College.
cues.zh: 帝国学院的病理学教授。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: she... I asked her, said, you know, I said, I want to... I'd like to present this, but I'm not a radiation scientist, so can I just steal your slides? I'll put your picture on them if you let me do that.
cues.zh: 她……我问她，我说，你知道的，我说，我想……我想展示这些，但我不是辐射科学家，所以我能借用你的幻灯片吗？如果你答应的话，我会把你的照片放上去。她指出的一件事是

cues.en: The first thing she points out is she says,
cues.zh: 她说，

cues.en: most ionizing radiation,
cues.zh: 绝大多数电离辐射——

cues.en: that's the radiation that is potentially harmful that comes from a nuclear accident,
cues.zh: 也就是核事故产生的、具有潜在危害的辐射——

cues.en: most of it is natural. And I was like, well, that sounds alright.
cues.zh: 大部分都是天然的。当时我想，好吧，听起来挺不错的。

cues.en: Like natural foods. Natural radiation sounds good. The hot springs, you know? And she said, no, actually natural
cues.zh: 就像天然食品一样。天然辐射听起来不错。比如温泉，你知道吗？她说，不，其实天然

cues.en: ionizing radiation is just as harmful potentially as artificial radiation. So that's kind of the first thing. The striking thing about it is that the total amount of ionizing radiation we're exposed to from not just Chernobyl and Fukushima,
cues.zh: 电离辐射和人造辐射一样具有潜在的危害。所以这是第一点。最引人注目的是，我们接触到的电离辐射总量，不仅来自切尔诺贝利和福岛，

cues.en: but also all of the atomic bomb testing in the sixties and seventies totals just point three percent of our exposures. Most of the radiation we're exposed to is just from the earth or from the atmosphere
cues.zh: 还来自六七十年代的所有原子弹试验，加起来只占我们受照剂量的百分之零点三。我们接触到的大多数辐射都只来自地球、大气层

cues.en: or from the buildings around us.
cues.zh: 或我们周围的建筑物。

cues.en: Let's look at the big one. This is Chernobyl. This is the event that really
cues.zh: 我们来看看最严重的一个。这就是切尔诺贝利。正是这个事件

cues.en: scared me about nuclear and led me to be an anti nuclear activist.
cues.zh: 真正让我对核能感到恐惧，并让我成为了一名反核活动人士。

cues.en: United Nations has done these very large comprehensive
cues.zh: 联合国做过非常大型、全面的

cues.en: studies. They have hundreds
cues.zh: 研究。他们有来自世界各地的

cues.en: of scientists around the world
cues.zh: 数百名科学家

cues.en: that do this research. So the possibility of somebody fudging the data or
cues.zh: 来开展这项研究。因此，在那种环境下，有人篡改数据或

cues.en: maybe trying to cover something up is pretty low in that environment just because there's so many different credit... Credible scientists at different universities around the world doing the research.
cues.zh: 试图掩盖什么的几率相当低，因为有太多不同的信誉……来自世界各地不同大学的权威科学家在进行这项研究。

cues.en: So this is really, I think was a pivotal moment for me.
cues.zh: 所以这真的、我认为对我来说是一个转折点。

cues.en: Chernobyl is the worst nuclear accident we've ever had. And I think there's some people that say it's the worst we could ever have. I don't need to make a statement that strong, but
cues.zh: 切尔诺贝利是我们经历过的最严重的核事故。而且我认为有人说这是我们可能遇到的最严重事故。我没必要下这么绝对的结论，但

cues.en: they literally had a nuclear reactor without a containment dome and it was on fire. Like it was like just
cues.zh: 他们居然建了一个没有安全壳的核反应堆，而且它还着火了。就像

cues.en: raining radiation
cues.zh: 辐射雨一样

cues.en: around everybody.
cues.zh: 洒在每个人周围。

cues.en: It was a really terrible accident. And when they start counting bodies,
cues.zh: 这是一场非常可怕的事故。而当他们开始统计死伤人数时，

cues.en: what they come up with is twenty eight deaths from acute radiation syndrome,
cues.zh: 他们得出的数字是：二十八人死于急性放射病，

cues.en: fifteen deaths over the last twenty five years from thyroid cancer, which as horrible as it sounds, it's actually the best cancer to get because hardly anybody dies from it. It's really treatable. You can take thyroxine, which is a synthetic substitute,
cues.zh: 过去二十五年中有十五人死于甲状腺癌。听起来很可怕，但其实这是最容易治愈的癌症，因为几乎没人会因此丧命。它真的很可治愈。你可以服用人工合成替代品左旋甲状腺素，

cues.en: get a surgery. In fact, most of the people that died were people that were in remote rural areas that couldn't get the medical treatment they needed.
cues.zh: 做个手术就行。事实上，大多数死者都是身处偏远农村地区、无法获得所需医疗救治的人。

cues.en: And if you take the
cues.zh: 如果把

cues.en: sixteen thousand
cues.zh: 一万六千

cues.en: people that got thyroid cancer from Chernobyl,
cues.zh: 名从切尔诺贝利得了甲状腺癌的人算进来，

cues.en: they estimate one hundred and sixty of them will die from thyroid cancer. And it's not like they're dying right now. They'll die of it in old age. And that's not to say that it's okay, but it is to put it in some kind of context.
cues.zh: 他们估计其中160人会死于甲状腺癌。而且并不是说他们现在就会死，他们会在年老时因此去世。这不是说这就没问题，而是为了把它放在某种背景下看。

cues.en: There's no scientific evidence of thyroid cancer outside of those three main countries, Belarus, Ukraine and Russia.
cues.zh: 除了白俄罗斯、乌克兰和俄罗斯这三个主要国家，没有科学证据表明出现甲状腺癌。

cues.en: No effect on fertility, malformations, infant mortality.
cues.zh: 对生育力、出生缺陷、婴儿死亡率没有影响。

cues.en: No data
cues.zh: 没有数据

cues.en: for adverse pregnancy outcomes.
cues.zh: 关于不良妊娠结局的。

cues.en: No evidence for any genetic effects.
cues.zh: 没有证据表明有任何遗传影响。

cues.en: And I think this last one is the most striking thing.
cues.zh: 我觉得最后这一点最令人震惊。

cues.en: There's no evidence of any increase in cancer,
cues.zh: 没有证据表明癌症有任何增加，

cues.en: including in the cohort of people who put the fire out and cleaned up afterwards.
cues.zh: 包括那些参与灭火和事后清理的人群。

cues.en: And I I still I say I still am surprised by this finding,
cues.zh: 我得说，我到现在还是对这个发现感到惊讶，

cues.en: and so I put the link to the website on there. I don't think you should take my word for it. I think you should go read it because just reading about Chernobyl for me was a big part of changing my mind about nuclear power.
cues.zh: 所以我把网站链接放在那里。我觉得你不该只听我说，我觉得你应该去读一读，因为对我来说，光是阅读切尔诺贝利的资料，就是改变我对核能看法的重要部分。

cues.en: What about Fukushima? This was also the second worst nuclear disaster in history.
cues.zh: 那福岛呢？这也是历史上第二严重的核灾难。

cues.en: It was a much smaller release of radiation than Chernobyl.
cues.zh: 它释放的辐射比切尔诺贝利少得多。

cues.en: And so what we find is that no deaths from radiation exposure from Fukushima, which is kind of amazing.
cues.zh: 所以我们发现，福岛没有因辐射暴露导致的死亡，这相当令人惊讶。

cues.en: Fifteen hundred people died being pulled out of nursing homes, being pulled out of hospitals.
cues.zh: 有一千五百人是在被从养老院、医院转移出来时死亡的。

cues.en: It was insane. It was a panic. The Japanese government should not have done that. It violated every standard of how you deal with like that. You're supposed to shelter in place. In fact, by pulling people out of their homes and moving them around outside during that accident, they actually exposed people to more radiation.
cues.zh: 那太疯狂了。简直是一场恐慌。日本政府不该那么做。这违背了处理这类事故的所有标准。你应该就地避难。事实上，在那次事故中，把人们从家里撤出来、让他们在外面四处移动，反而使他们暴露在了更多辐射之下。

cues.en: And and of course you have to put that in comparison to the other things that were going on, like fifteen to twenty thousand people dying instantly from drowning, pinned under many different technologies by the way, getting killed by that tsunami.
cues.zh: 当然，你还得把这件事和其他同时发生的情况做个对比，比如一万五到两万人瞬间被淹死，顺便说一句，他们是被各种不同的技术压在下面，被那场海啸夺去生命的。

cues.en: Unlikely to an increase in thyroid cancer
cues.zh: 不太可能导致甲状腺癌增加

cues.en: and the big problems of course is just the stress and the fear that you've got. You've been contaminated when the evidence suggests that that's not the case at all.
cues.zh: 当然，最大的问题就是你感受到的压力和恐惧。你已经被污染了——而证据表明根本不是这么回事。

cues.en: They did an interesting study. They brought a bunch of school kids from Paris
cues.zh: 他们做了一项有趣的研究。他们带了一群来自巴黎的学童

cues.en: to Fukushima and they wore dosimeters.
cues.zh: 到福岛，让他们佩戴剂量计。

cues.en: That's what we call the old Geiger counters now.
cues.zh: 这就是我们现在所说的老式盖革计数器。

cues.en: And what they find is that those kids, when they go through the security systems, the radiation would spike. When they'd get on the airplane to fly to Tokyo, the radiation would spike.
cues.zh: 结果他们发现，那些孩子经过安检系统时，辐射读数会飙升。登上飞往东京的飞机时，辐射读数会飙升。

cues.en: They go to the French embassy, the radiation would spike.
cues.zh: 他们去法国大使馆，辐射读数会飙升。

cues.en: Awakee didn't get... Awakee is a city and it didn't get the
cues.zh: Awakee没有受到……Awakee是一座城市，它没有受到

cues.en: the plume, the radioactive plume.
cues.zh: 那团烟羽，放射性烟羽的影响。

cues.en: Tomioka did, and it's still a tiny blip compared to just going through the security system.
cues.zh: 富冈受到了影响，但和仅仅经过安检系统相比，那仍然只是微不足道的一点点。

cues.en: So let's look at some of the basics to put this in context. If you live in a big city like London or Berlin
cues.zh: 那么让我们来看一些基础知识，以便更好地理解背景。如果你住在伦敦或柏林这样的大城市

cues.en: or
cues.zh: 或者

cues.en: New York, you're gonna increase your mortality risk by two point eight percent just from air pollution alone. If you live with someone who smokes cigarettes,
cues.zh: 纽约，仅空气污染一项就会让你的死亡风险增加2.8%。如果你和吸烟的人同住，

cues.en: one point seven percent. But if you were somebody that cleaned up Chernobyl,
cues.zh: 百分之之一点七。但如果你是当年清理切尔诺贝利的人，

cues.en: got exposed to 250
cues.zh: 接触到了 250

cues.en: millisieverts
cues.zh: 毫西弗

cues.en: of radiation,
cues.zh: 辐射的，

cues.en: one percent. A 100 millisieverts,
cues.zh: 百分之一。100 毫西弗，

cues.en: point four percent.
cues.zh: 零点四。

cues.en: And it's just because there just wasn't as much radiation as people think. I mean, the atomic bomb testing in the sixties exposed people to just... There's so many different measurements for radiation. You can just see a lot more radiation exposure
cues.zh: 而这只是因为辐射根本没有人们以为的那么多。我是说，六十年代的原子弹试验让人们接触到的……关于辐射有太多不同的测量方式。你完全可以看到多得多的辐射暴露。

cues.en: during the a bomb test than either Chernobyl or Fukushima.
cues.zh: 在原子弹测试期间，其影响超过了切尔诺贝利或福岛。

cues.en: I think the key thing here is I'm from the state of Colorado in The United States. We have an annual exposure just because there's so much granite around us, about nine millisieverts a year. That's what you would get if you are the 6,000,000 people that live around Chernobyl today.
cues.zh: 我想关键的一点是，我来自美国科罗拉多州。因为我们周围有大量的花岗岩，所以每年受到的辐射暴露大约是9毫西弗。而今天生活在切尔诺贝利周围的600万人，他们所受到的辐射量也就是这个水平。

cues.en: And yet, of course, nobody knows this. Like here's this really basic science, it's right there on the website, but when you go and do a survey in most countries, this one was done in Russia,
cues.zh: 然而，当然，根本没人知道这一点。就像这里有一个非常基础的科学知识，它就明摆在网站上，但当你去大多数国家做调查时——这项是在俄罗斯做的——

cues.en: only 8%
cues.zh: 只有 8%

cues.en: of the population that surveyed
cues.zh: 在接受调查的人群中

cues.en: accurately predicts the death toll
cues.zh: 准确预测死亡人数

cues.en: from Chernobyl
cues.zh: 来自切尔诺贝利

cues.en: and 0%
predicted accurately the death toll from Fukushima.
cues.zh: 准确预测了福岛核事故的死亡人数。

cues.en: Meanwhile,
cues.zh: 与此同时，

cues.en: sitting right before us is seven million deaths a year from air pollution and the evidence on particulate matter causing harm has only gotten stronger over the years.
cues.zh: 我们眼前每年有七百万人死于空气污染，而且多年来关于颗粒物危害的证据也越来越确凿。

cues.en: So that's why every major medical journal that looks at this, this is from the British medical journal Lancet, finds that nuclear power is already the safest way to make electricity.
cues.zh: 所以这就是为什么所有关注此事的顶级医学期刊——这份来自英国医学杂志《柳叶刀》——都发现核能已经是发电最安全的方式。

cues.en: And it leads to this really uncomfortable conclusion,
cues.zh: 这也引出了一个非常让人难受的结论，

cues.en: one that the climate scientist James Hansen
cues.zh: 气候科学家James Hansen

cues.en: came to recently, which is that
cues.zh: 最近得出的结论，那就是

cues.en: nuclear power has actually saved one point eight million lives.
cues.zh: 核能实际上已经拯救了一百八十万人的生命。

cues.en: It's not something that you hear very much about.
cues.zh: 这并不是那种你经常能听到的说法。

cues.en: So what about the waste? Well, this is the waste from a nuclear plant in The United States. The thing about the nuclear waste is it's the only waste from electricity production that is safely contained anywhere. All of the other waste goes into the environment,
cues.zh: 那么废料怎么办呢？你看，这是美国一家核电站的废料。核废料的特点在于，它是所有发电废料中唯一被妥善收容的。而所有其他废料都直接排入了环境中，

cues.en: from coal,
cues.zh: 比如煤炭，

cues.en: gas,
cues.zh: 天然气，

cues.en: and then here's sort of a... Equally
cues.zh: 还有下面这个……同样

cues.en: uncomfortable conclusion,
cues.zh: 让人难受的结论，

cues.en: Solar panels.
cues.zh: 太阳能面板。

cues.en: There's no plan to recycle solar panels outside of the EU,
cues.zh: 除了欧盟之外，目前没有任何回收太阳能面板的计划，

cues.en: meaning that all of us in California,
cues.zh: 这意味着我们在加利福尼亚的所有人，

cues.en: it's just going to join the waste stream. We calculated, well, how much toxic waste... Because the panels contain heavy metals and lead and chromium and cadmium. How much toxic waste from solar is there?
cues.zh: 这些面板最终都将进入垃圾流。我们计算过，究竟有多少有毒废物……因为面板含有重金属、铅、铬和镉。太阳能会产生多少有毒废物？

cues.en: Well, to get a sense of it, look at how much more materials are required for each different energy source.
cues.zh: 为了让你有个直观感受，看看每种不同的能源需要消耗多少倍的材料就知道了。

cues.en: And when you calculate all the panels that are required to produce the same amount of electricity as nuclear,
cues.zh: 而当你计算需要多少块太阳能板才能发出与核能相同的电量时，

cues.en: solar actually produces 300 times more waste than nuclear,
cues.zh: 太阳能产生的废物实际上比核能多300倍，

cues.en: very little of it contained,
cues.zh: 其中很少被妥善封存，

cues.en: and all of it containing toxic heavy metals.
cues.zh: 而且全都含有有毒重金属。

cues.en: What about the weapons? If I thought there was any chance that more nuclear power would increase the chance of nuclear war, I would be against it. I've always been a pacifist. I still am. Diplomacy is always, almost always the right solution.
cues.zh: 那武器问题呢？如果我认为增加核电有任何可能增加核战争的风险，我就会反对它。我一直是个和平主义者。现在依然是。外交几乎永远是正确解决方案。

cues.en: Well, people say, what about North Korea?
cues.zh: 嗯，人们会问，那朝鲜呢？

cues.en: Korea proves the point. In order to get nuclear power right now, I mean, it's been this way for fifty years, you have to agree not to get a weapon. That's the deal. South Korea wanted nuclear power. They agreed not to get a weapon. They don't have a weapon. North Korea wanted nuclear power. I think they should have gotten it. We didn't let them have it for a variety of reasons.
cues.zh: 朝鲜恰恰证明了这一点。要想获得核能——我是说，五十年来一直如此——你必须同意不获取武器。这就是交易。韩国想要核能。他们同意不获取武器。他们没有武器。朝鲜想要核能。我认为他们本该得到它。出于种种原因，我们没让他们拥有。

cues.en: They got a bomb. They now are testing missiles that can hit Japan. They can hit...
cues.zh: 他们搞到了炸弹。他们现在在测试能打到日本的导弹。他们能打到……

cues.en: Soon they'll be able to hit California.
cues.zh: 很快他们就能打到加利福尼亚。

cues.en: So if nuclear energy led to nuclear bombs, it's no evidence for it, not only in Korea but nowhere.
cues.zh: 所以如果说核能会导致核弹，那无论在朝鲜还是其他地方都没有证据支持。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: where does that leave us? Well, I think it leaves us with some uncomfortable ideas. I mean, if Germany hadn't closed its nuclear plants,
cues.zh: 这让我们处于什么境地？嗯，我认为这给我们留下了一些令人不安的结论。我是说，如果德国没有关闭它的核电站，

cues.en: its emissions would be 43% lower than it is today.
cues.zh: 它的排放量会比今天低43%。

cues.en: And I think if you care about climate change, that's at least something that you have to wrestle with, especially in light of some of these facts about the harms and benefits of different energy sources. And I'll end with a quote from somebody else who changed his mind and somebody else who was a huge childhood hero for me.
cues.zh: 我觉得如果你关心气候变化，这至少是你必须去面对的问题，特别是结合不同能源利弊的这些事实来看。最后我引用另一个改变了想法的人的话，他也是我童年时极度崇拜的英雄。

cues.en: And that's STING.
cues.zh: 那就是 STING。

cues.en: If you're gonna tackle global warming, nuclear is the only way you can create massive amounts of power.
cues.zh: 如果要应对全球变暖，核能是你唯一能产生巨量电力的方式。

cues.en: Thank you very much. Appreciate you listening.
cues.zh: 非常感谢。谢谢你们的倾听。
